# Orrery: guide for AI agents

Pinned to: **orrery 0.0.1** | ERP 1 | MCP 2025-06-18 | build id `0xcedc48d20b374474` | game `PhysGame` | schema fingerprint `0xcd80fb0371ad0307`

If the host you talk to reports a different version, build id or schema fingerprint (`orr status`, `orr schema --types`), this file may be out of date: trust the host and regenerate the file with `orr agents-md`.

## What Orrery is

Orrery is a deterministic, rollback-capable ECS game engine. A **scene** is a set of **entities** (each with a stable GUID such as `e_00000005` and an optional display name) that carry **components**, plus **singletons** (one value per type). The simulation uses fixed-point arithmetic only, so the same scene and the same inputs always produce the same checksums on every machine. That is what makes verification by replay exact.

You work with the `orr` command line, a thin client of a running host (the editor, or the headless `orr_remote_host`) over ERP. Your edits go through the same document as a person's: they share one undo history, and each entry says who made it (`agent:<your client name>`). A person watching the editor sees what you do in its Agent tab; there is no approval step, so finish the job yourself: check your change with `orr apply` and undo what turns out wrong.

## Setup

Start a host (once), then use `orr` from any shell:

```sh
orr_editor --erp 127.0.0.1:7777 --erp-dev          # the editor, with an ERP endpoint (no token: local development)
orr_remote_host --dev-no-auth                        # or headless, same address
orr_remote_host --token claude:s3cret:all             # a host that needs a token (name:token:capabilities)
orr status                                            # is it there? game, mode, tick, checksum, proposals
```

- Address: `--erp <url>` or `ORR_ERP` (also accepted: `ORR_ERP_URL`), default `ws://127.0.0.1:7777`.
- Token: `--token <t>` or `ORR_ERP_TOKEN` (prefer the environment: it stays out of the process list). No token = a host started in dev mode. `orr` never prints the token.
- `--json` on any command prints the raw structured result instead of text. `--name <agent>` is informational; the host's token decides the name in the history.
- `orr help` lists the commands; `orr help <command>` (or `orr <command> --help`) documents one with examples.

## The workflow

1. **Look first.** `orr status`; `orr scene` (entities, GUIDs, component types; `--filter <text>`, `--has <Type>`, `--components` for values); `orr get <entity> [Component.path]` (an entity is a GUID or an exact display name); `orr schema --types` and `orr schema <type>` for fields, ranges and docs. Never guess a GUID or a field name.
2. **Small edits: `orr set`.** `orr set body_05 Body.pos=[6,18] Body.angle=0.5` changes the scene at once; all assignments of one command are one undo entry. Also `orr spawn`, `orr despawn`, `orr rename`, `orr add`, `orr remove`.
3. **Anything non-trivial: `orr apply`.** `orr apply "lift hero" set hero Body.pos=[6,18] --check "lost_bodies.max == 0"` stages the change on a private copy, replays the scene without and with it on the same inputs, judges your `--check` rules and accepts the change only if all pass. On a failed check it rejects the change, prints the report and exits 4 with the scene untouched (`--keep` leaves the proposal open to fix). This is the recommended way to change a scene.
4. **Step by step, when you need to look between the steps:** `orr propose <label> <ops...>` (nothing changes; prints the diff), `orr verify <pN> --check ...`, then `orr accept <pN>` or `orr reject <pN>`. `orr proposals` and `orr diff <pN>` show what is open; a person may make proposals too.
5. **Watch and undo.** `orr activity` (or `orr activity -f` to follow live) shows what every client did, with old and new values. `orr history` lists the undo history; `orr undo` takes the last entry back exactly, whoever made it; `orr redo` repeats it.

Do not accept or apply what you have not verified. Keep changes small and focused, with a label that says what and why: the label becomes the history entry.

## Commands

| Command | What it does | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| `orr status` | host, game, build id, mode (edit or play), tick, checksum, unsaved changes, open proposals, connected clients | `read` |
| `orr scene [--components] [--filter t] [--has Type]` | entities and singletons | `read` |
| `orr get <entity> [Component[.path]]` | values in the scene format (`@Scene` reads a singleton) | `read` |
| `orr schema [type] \| --types` | the value schema of the game's types | `read` |
| `orr set <entity> Comp.path=value ...` | direct edit, one undo entry | `scene_edit` |
| `orr spawn [--name n] [Comp=json ...]`, `despawn`, `rename`, `add`, `remove` | direct edits | `scene_edit` |
| `orr apply <label> <ops...> --check <rule>` | propose, verify, accept if all checks pass (else reject, exit 4) | `scene_edit`, `approve` |
| `orr propose <label> <ops...>` | stage a proposal, print its diff (scene unchanged) | `scene_edit` |
| `orr verify [<pN>] [--bot N \| --idle N \| --last-play \| --replay f] [--check rule]` | replay check of a proposal, or the baseline of the scene | `read` |
| `orr accept <pN>` / `orr reject <pN>` / `orr proposals` / `orr diff <pN>` | decide and inspect proposals | `approve` / `scene_edit` / `read` |
| `orr history [-n N]`, `orr undo`, `orr redo` | the undo history | `read`, `scene_edit` |
| `orr sim start\|stop\|play\|pause\|step [N]\|seek <tick>\|speed <x>\|state` | a play session (a copy: the scene document is untouched) | `sim_control` |
| `orr activity [--since seq] [--reads] [-f]` | the activity feed of the host | `read` |
| `orr save [--write]` | scene YAML to stdout, or write the host's scene file | `read` / `scene_edit` |
| `orr agents-md` | this guide, generated from the host | `read` |

Ops (for `apply`, `propose`; `set` and friends are the same words as commands):

```text
set <entity> <Comp.path>=<value>...       sset <Singleton.path>=<value>...
rename <entity> <name>                    despawn <entity>
add <entity> <Comp> [json]                remove <entity> <Comp>
spawn [--name n] [Comp=<json>...]
```

Or a JSON list of op objects from `--ops-file ops.json`, or from stdin with `-`: `{"op":"patch","entity":"e_00000005","component":"orr_physics::Body","path":"pos","value":[0,12.5]}` (also `insert`, `remove`, `spawn`, `despawn`, `rename`, `singleton.patch`). Example: `orr propose "lift hero" set hero Body.pos=[6,18] rename body_05 hero`.

An entity is a GUID or an exact display name (an ambiguous name is an error that lists the matches: use a GUID). A component may be written by its short name when that is unambiguous (`Body.pos` for `orr_physics::Body.pos`); an ambiguous short name is an error that lists the candidates.

## Value format

Values follow the scene file and `registry.schema`: bool = true/false; integer = JSON number; fixed-point = JSON number with its exact decimal text (never rounded through a float; the server accepts a number or a string with the same text, an exponent, and rounds extra digits to 1/65536); vec2/vec3 = [x, y] / [x, y, z]; entity reference = GUID string `e_7f3a91c2` or null (`12v0` handle text for entities created during play); enum = variant name; flags = array of names; struct = object with all fields (a whole-component write may leave fields out: they take the type default); tagged value = object with `kind`. u64 checksums are strings `0x` + 16 hex digits.

On the command line a value is parsed as JSON when it is JSON, else as a bare decimal (`.5`, `+3`) or string: `pos=[6,18]`, `angle=0.5`, `orr_physics::Body.kind=dynamic`, `target=null`, `mask="7"` (quote to force a string). Quote arguments that contain spaces or brackets for your shell.

Examples: a vector `[0, 12.5]`; a fixed-point number `-0.5` (write it as a plain decimal, never in quotes); an enum `dynamic`; an entity reference `e_00000005` or `null`; a tagged value `{ "kind": "circle", "radius": 0.5 }`. Numbers come back exact: `0.1` is stored as `0.1000061` (1/65536 steps), and a checksum is a string `0x` followed by 16 hex digits.

## Types of this game

Every field is required in the scene file, but a whole-component patch may list only some fields (the rest stay). `orr schema <type>` gives the exact schema of one type.

### `PaddleTag` (component)

Marks the paddle of a player.

- `slot`: int [0, 4294967295]

### `Scene` (singleton)

Scene constants, set once in `setup`.

- `half_w`: fixed
- `height`: fixed
- `spawn_batch`: int [0, 4294967295]
- `spawn_interval`: int [0, 4294967295]. Ticks between spawns; 0 = never.
- `max_entities`: int [0, 4294967295]
- `mode`: int [0, 4294967295]

### `orr_physics::Body` (component)

Dynamics state of one body. Attach together with a [`Collider`]. `inv_mass` / `inv_inertia` are ignored (treated as 0) unless `kind == BODY_DYNAMIC`.

- `pos`: vec2 [-30000, 30000]. World position of the center of mass.
- `angle`: fixed [-3.1416, 3.1416]. Rotation in radians, kept in `(-pi, pi]` by the integrator.
- `vel`: vec2 [-500, 500]. Linear velocity.
- `omega`: fixed [-60, 60]. Angular velocity (rad/s).
- `inv_mass`: fixed [0, 1000]. Inverse mass (0 = immovable).
- `inv_inertia`: fixed [0, 100000]. Inverse rotational inertia (0 = fixed rotation).
- `linear_damping`: fixed [0, 100]. Per-second linear velocity damping (0 = none).
- `angular_damping`: fixed [0, 100]. Per-second angular velocity damping (0 = none).
- `kind`: one of `static` | `dynamic` | `kinematic`. [`BODY_STATIC`], [`BODY_DYNAMIC`] or [`BODY_KINEMATIC`].

### `orr_physics::Collider` (component)

Collision shape and material of one body.

- `shape`: tagged by `kind`: `circle` {radius}; `box` {half_extents}; `polygon` {verts}; `capsule` {half_length, radius}; `capsule_segment` {a, b, radius}. Local shape.
- `restitution`: fixed [0, 1]. Bounciness in `[0, 1]`. Pairs use the larger value.
- `friction`: fixed [0, 100]. Coulomb friction coefficient. Pairs use the geometric mean.
- `layer`: int [0, 4294967295]. Layer bits of this collider.
- `mask`: int [0, 4294967295]. Layers this collider can touch. A pair collides only if each one's `layer` intersects the other's `mask`.
- `flags`: list of one of `sensor`. [`COLLIDER_SENSOR`] bit.

### `orr_physics::PhysicsState` (singleton)

Singleton holding the config and the persistent (rollback-safe) caches.

- `config`: object. Solver settings.

## Verification

`orr verify` (and `orr apply`) run both scenes for a number of ticks on **inputs**:

| inputs | meaning |
|---|---|
| `--bot 300 [--seed 1] [--players 2]` | scripted players (deterministic; another seed, another play). The default. |
| `--idle 300` | no player input |
| `--last-play` | the recording of the last play session stopped in this host (a person's play in the editor, or `orr sim`) |
| `--replay file.orrp` | a recording file |

Limits: at most 6000 simulation ticks per call. One verification runs off the host thread at a time; other requests and play continue. A second verification returns `verify_busy`. Reports describe the scene/proposal captured at admission; guarded acceptance rejects later changes. The tick cap does not bound replay decoding memory or elapsed time. Tick rate 60, 2 players by default. Scripted players: available.

Every scene edit changes the checksums from tick 0, so `first_divergence` is 0 for a real change. **Judge behaviour by metrics and checks**, not by divergence. An unchanged run (`identical: true`) means the change has no effect on the simulation.

### Checks

Repeat `--check "<rule>"` for each rule; the exit code is 4 when any fails.

Grammar: `<metric>[.start|final|min|max|delta] <|<=|==|!=|>=|> <number> | base:<metric>... | no_divergence | no_divergence_before <tick> | recording_matches`

- `<metric>.<stat> <cmp> <number>`: `stat` is `start` (before the first tick), `final` (after the last; the default), `min`, `max` (over the sampled ticks) or `delta` (candidate final minus base final). `cmp` is `<`, `<=`, `==`, `!=`, `>=` or `>`. A metric of the candidate run unless prefixed `base:`.
- `no_divergence`: checksums equal at every tick. `no_divergence_before <tick>`. `recording_matches`: the scene reproduces the recording's checksums (`--last-play` or `--replay`).

Examples: `lost_bodies.max == 0`, `mean_height >= 2.5`, `base:dynamic_bodies.start == 40`, `kinetic_energy.delta <= 10`, `entities.final == 49`.

`orr verify` without a proposal runs the scene alone: baseline numbers to choose sensible thresholds from. `orr apply` without `--check` uses `lost_bodies.max == 0` if the game reports that metric, else judges nothing.

### Metrics

Integer (`int`) or exact fixed-point (`fixed`) numbers sampled during the run.

| metric | kind |
|---|---|
| `entities` | int |
| `dynamic_bodies` | int |
| `sleeping_bodies` | int |
| `lost_bodies` | int |
| `mean_height` | fixed |
| `max_height` | fixed |
| `min_height` | fixed |
| `max_speed` | fixed |
| `kinetic_energy` | fixed |

`components.<type>` (int) counts the entities that have a component type: `PaddleTag`, `orr_physics::Body`, `orr_physics::Collider`.

## Exit codes and errors

| code | meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | ok |
| 1 | the command failed: the host answered with an error (unknown entity or type, invalid value, conflict, missing capability, ...) |
| 2 | usage error: the command line is wrong (`orr help <command>`) |
| 3 | cannot connect or authenticate (no host at the address, wrong token) |
| 4 | checks failed (`orr verify`, `orr apply`) |

Errors go to stderr as `error: <message>` with a hint what to do; results go to stdout. A failed `orr apply` (exit 4) has already rejected its proposal and changed nothing; a failed `orr set` changed nothing either (its edits are one transaction).

## Capabilities

A host gives each token a set of capabilities; a command refused for lack of one says which (exit 1).

| capability | allows |
|---|---|
| `read` | look at the scene, schema, proposals, history, activity; verify (replay runs on copies) |
| `scene_edit` | edit the scene, make and change proposals, reject them, undo |
| `approve` | accept a proposal into the scene (`orr accept`, and the last step of `orr apply`) |
| `sim_control` | start, step, seek and stop a play session |

If your token lacks `approve`, `orr apply` stops after a passing verification and leaves the proposal open for a person to accept in the editor.

## Conventions and pitfalls

- Prefer GUIDs (from `orr scene`) in scripts: display names are not unique, and a rename changes them.
- Stay inside the ranges the schema states; an out-of-range or mistyped value is refused with the field named.
- Despawning an entity that another entity still points at is refused: change the reference first (same `apply`).
- While a play session runs (`orr sim`), the scene document cannot be accepted into or undone; `orr sim stop` first.
- `orr save --write` overwrites the host's scene file: do it only when asked to keep the change.

## MCP alternative

For clients without a shell, the same engine is available as an MCP server (`orr_mcp`, stdio) with the same workflow: `claude mcp add orrery -- orr_mcp --erp ws://127.0.0.1:7777 --token ...` (or `ORR_ERP_TOKEN` in the environment). The tools call the same ERP methods as `orr` and produce the same reports:

Tool groups on in this guide: scene, propose, verify, sim, history. (`orr_mcp --tools scene,propose,verify` switches groups on and off.)

| Tool | Group | Needs | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `scene_overview` | scene | `read` | List the entities of the scene (GUID, display name, component types) and the singletons, with counts. |
| `get_entity` | scene | `read` | Read the components of one entity: all of them, one component, or one field. |
| `get_schema` | scene | `read` | The JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) of the scene format: every component and singleton type with its fields, ranges and docs. |
| `propose_changes` | propose | `scene_edit` | Stage a set of edits as a PROPOSAL. |
| `list_proposals` | propose | `read` | List the open proposals (id, label, who made it, number of ops, whether the scene changed since). |
| `accept_proposal` | propose | `approve` | Apply a proposal to the scene as ONE undoable history entry (recorded as made by whoever proposed it). |
| `reject_proposal` | propose | `scene_edit` | Discard a proposal (for example after verify_proposal failed). |
| `verify_proposal` | verify | `read` | Check a proposal by REPLAY: the engine runs the scene without and with the proposal, headlessly and deterministically, on the same inputs, and compares checksums and metrics. |
| `sim_run` | sim | `sim_control` | Drive a play session of the scene (a copy: the scene document is untouched). |
| `history` | history | `read` | The undo history of the scene, oldest first: id, label, who made it (`user` or `agent:<name>`), number of ops, whether undone. |
| `undo` | history | `scene_edit` | Take back the last history entry (whoever made it; a whole accepted proposal at once). |

Resources: `orrery://scene` (the scene as YAML), `orrery://schema` (JSON Schema), `orrery://agents` (this guide). A tool that fails returns `isError: true` with the engine's message. Ids are strings: proposals `p1`, entities `e_...`. The MCP workflow is `scene_overview`, `get_entity`, `get_schema`, then `propose_changes`, `verify_proposal` with `checks`, `accept_proposal` (needs `approve`), `undo`; `sim_run` drives a play session. Verification inputs are JSON there: `{"kind":"bot","ticks":300,"seed":1}`, `{"kind":"idle","ticks":300}`, `{"kind":"last_play"}`, `{"kind":"replay","base64":"..."}`.
